license.payload: Per item, recorded in origin.items. The works are medieval (al-Khwārizmī d. c. 850; al-Kindī d. c. 873; Thābit ibn Qurra d. 901; Ibn al-Haytham d. c. 1040; al-Bīrūnī d. c. 1050; ʿUmar al-Khayyām d. 1131) and in the public domain. Rosen's edition (London, 1831; the Arabic title page dated 1830) and Woepcke's (Paris, 1851) are public domain in the United States (published before 1931); the Archive marks the Google and California copies NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT and the Arabic-part item Public Domain Mark 1.0. The OpenITI files are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 at the corpus: handled under the NC payload/record split ruled at EA-CORPORA-02, as GRETIL was at 29/09 — the NonCommercial payload licence is carried forward unmodified and does not attach to this seat record. Most OpenITI files transcribe or OCR printed editions of 1889 to the 2000s, named per item in origin.items (edition_at_file); OpenITI's Clean operation of 2023 removed editorial paratext from the OCR files, though some introductions remain in the text. Edition-level status for the editions printed after 1930 is recorded as UNVERIFIED AT SEAT TIME: the medieval text is the author's, and the seat claims no more for the edition than the OpenITI licence gives. The Majisṭī file is a transcription of a manuscript (Tunis 7116), with no printed edition behind it.

normalization: Originals as fetched under original/: Internet Archive scans with their OCR layers; OpenITI mARkdown files from raw.githubusercontent.com pinned to the repository commit (0275AH at 44e1c36738a2bf5c14dafa232a6ae1891e6171cd, 0300AH at 01a1544130e0236850ef2698923ad01575c5bd7c, 0450AH at 8b80029191e1b7a8809d812ec6186df862e18217). text/<slug>.ocr.txt is the Archive's OCR with line endings normalized. text/<slug>.txt is the OpenITI file reduced by code (openiti30.py): the metadata header dropped, headings marked, '~~' continuation lines joined, page markers kept as [V01P001], milestones dropped. The Kraken OCR files are uncorrected OCR as OpenITI publishes them. No text was corrected by hand.
scope: Arabic only, in six authors. al-Khwārizmī's Algebra in Rosen's Arabic (London, 1831), held twice: the whole book, Arabic and English, and the Arabic part scanned on its own, which the Archive labels “1342” and whose title page, dated London 1830, shows it to be Rosen's. The Archive's OCR of the whole book does not read its Arabic pages; the separate scan carries a Tesseract Arabic OCR. al-Kindī: three scientific treatises (music, the mathematics of compound drugs, swords). Thābit ibn Qurra: his Arabic Apollonius (Conics V) and Nicomachus, the Arabic Almagest he revised (in a manuscript transcription), and two works of his own astronomy. Ibn al-Haytham: the Optics in two OpenITI versions, Sabra's books I–III and the al-Warrāq text, and On the Configuration of the World. al-Bīrūnī: fourteen works of astronomy, mathematics and calendar, from the Masudic Canon to two fragments extant inside other treatises. ʿUmar al-Khayyām's Algebra in Woepcke's edition of 1851, two copies; its Arabic text pages stand in the scans, and the OCR reads only Woepcke's French. Held out: al-Kindī's Rasāʾil falsafiyya and Fī l-ʿaql and Fī l-nawm wa-l-ruʾyā (philosophy, outside the scientific works asked for); Thābit's Kitāb al-Rawābīʿ li-Aflāṭūn (a Hermetic work attributed to him); al-Bīrūnī's al-Jamāhir (mineralogy), al-Ṣaydana (pharmacology), Fihrist and Taḥqīq mā li-l-Hind (on India, with its astronomy inside a larger ethnography). Ibn al-Haytham's other mathematical works (on the quadrature, on Euclid's postulates) are not in OpenITI at the commits read.

why_seated: The exact sciences in the language that carried them from the Greeks to the Latins. al-jabr names the operation of restoring what was taken from one side of an equation, and Rosen's book of 1831 brought it back to Europe in its first Arabic print. The seat sets the founding Algebra beside Thābit's Arabic Euclideans, Ibn al-Haytham's Optics and al-Bīrūnī's instruments, so the line from the translation movement to the solution of the cubic by Khayyām can be read in one place.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-10-30: “and then an ea-corpora seating... Einstein, Gödel, Tesla, Copernicus, Galileo, classical Arabic mathematicians... what is in the public domain, and what else? and just to be perverse lets seat the promised Klee notebooks with them”; to the proposed set: “yes, thats a good set”.
